output.title: Expedited Prior Authorization Decision Timeframe
output.draft_text:
Q: How long does an expedited prior authorization decision take?

A: When a prior authorization request qualifies for expedited (urgent) review, a decision is made within [expedited decision timeframe, e.g., number of hours] of receiving [the request / all required clinical information]. A request typically qualifies for expedited review when [criteria for expedited review, e.g., prescriber attests that waiting for a standard decision could seriously jeopardize the member's life, health, or ability to regain maximum function].

How to request expedited review: [who can request expedited review, e.g., prescriber and/or member] can request it by [submission method(s), e.g., phone, fax, ePA portal], with [required documentation or attestation].

When the clock starts: The timeframe begins [clock start point, e.g., when the request is received / when all required information is received]. If information is missing, [process and effect on timeframe when information is incomplete].

If the request does not qualify: If expedited review is not approved, the request is processed under the standard timeframe of [standard decision timeframe], and [notification process when expedited request is downgraded].

How the decision is communicated: The prescriber and member are notified by [notification method(s)] within [notification timeframe, if different from decision timeframe].

If the decision is late: [what happens if the decision timeframe is missed, if applicable].

Applies to: [plan types / lines of business this timeframe applies to, e.g., commercial, Medicare Part D, Medicaid]. Timeframes may differ by plan type and state requirements; see [reference source or link].

author_checklist: Confirm the expedited prior authorization decision timeframe and its unit (hours vs. business/calendar days).
Confirm whether the timeframe differs by line of business (commercial, Medicare Part D, Medicaid) or by state, and list each applicable timeframe.
Confirm the criteria a request must meet to qualify for expedited review and who makes that determination.
Confirm who may request expedited review (prescriber, member, authorized representative) and the accepted submission channels.
Confirm when the timeframe clock starts and how missing or incomplete information affects it.
Confirm the standard (non-expedited) timeframe and the process and notification when an expedited request is downgraded.
Confirm how and when the prescriber and member are notified of the decision.
Confirm what happens if the decision is not made within the required timeframe (e.g., escalation or automatic outcome), if applicable.
Verify all timeframes against current regulatory requirements and internal policy documents, and cite the source.
Remove any placeholder sections that do not apply before approval.
